system_prompt_style.note: The repository bundle is karpathy/autoresearch, not the ResearchArena harness, so no prompt-construction code is available. The paper describes short per-stage guidelines but not how the prompt is assembled.

env_context_strategy.note: There is no harness code or config. Reviewers are said to inspect the workspace, which suggests agent-driven navigation by the underlying CLI agents, but this is not a stated mechanism.

context_compaction.note: No harness code; compaction would be handled by the wrapped CLI agents and is not described.

tool_call_format.note: Tool calling is done by the off-the-shelf CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code) and is not described.

tool_count.note: No tool registry in the evidence.

protocol_standardization.note: No source or dependency list for ResearchArena.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: each agent receives a CS-domain seed and runs a four-stage research loop: ideation, experiments, paper writing, and review. Stages 1–3 each include a self-refinement loop.
loop_primitives.note: The stages form a fixed pipeline. The per-stage self-refinement may be generate/refine, but it is not described mechanistically. The inner loop belongs to the wrapped CLI agent.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: The guidelines are intentionally kept short so they act as minimal scaffolding rather than as a step-by-step recipe.
planning_granularity.note: An experimental plan is written during ideation (Sec. 5.2), but no harness-stored plan object is described.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: a single off-the-shelf agent operates autonomously across broader computer science domains, rather than a pipeline of stage-specific components
multi_agent_topology.note: The review stage uses three reviewer agents, which is separate from the authoring run.

delegation_mechanism.note: No harness code to confirm the absence of delegation.

human_in_loop.note: Human inspection is post-hoc evaluation, not in-loop gating. There is no config surface.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Stages 1–3 each include a self-refinement loop.
self_verification.note: The Stage 4 SAR/PR reviews are evaluation, not feedback into the run.

retry_policy.note: Each paper gets 3 trials per agent-domain pair, but these are evaluation repeats, not retries. No config is available.

termination_condition.note: A time budget is mentioned in Sec. 5.2, but its enforcement is not described.

cost_controls.note: The paper reports a total cost of about $1,000, but no budget mechanism is described.

timeouts.note: The paper states agents are 'aware of the resources (i.e., hardware and time budget)', but no enforcement is described.

execution_isolation.note: Only the hardware is described; no execution boundary is given.

filesystem_access.note: Reviewer agents get read-only workspace access (Sec. 3.4). The authoring agent's access is not described.

network_policy.note: Reviewers do online lookups, but no network config is present in the evidence.

tracing.note: Logs and artifacts are released, but the tracing mechanism is not described.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: Stage 4 evaluates the resulting paper through three complementary lenses: the Stanford Agentic Reviewer (SAR, manuscript-only), our artifacts-aware peer review (PR, in which three agents inspect the workspace alongside the manuscript), and human inspection.
eval_hooks.note: This is paper-level only; the repository is not available to verify it.

target_domain.evidence_quote: lets off-the-shelf agents (Claude Code using Opus 4.6, Codex using GPT-5.4, and Kimi Code using K2.5) carry out the full research loop themselves

open_source.note: The paper says it releases 'the configurable harness', but no repo or licence is in the evidence. The bundled repo, karpathy/autoresearch (MIT), is a different system.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: Claude Code with Opus 4.6 [2], Codex with GPT-5.4 [13], and Kimi Code with K2.5 [ 11]
model_agnostic.note: The harness wraps multiple vendors' CLI agents; there is no litellm-style abstraction shown.

primary_artifact.note: The repository evidence supplied (karpathy/autoresearch) is not the ResearchArena harness. It is cited in the paper as related work [9].

first_release_date.note: The date is the paper v1 date, used as the fallback because no ResearchArena repo or tag is available.

pinned_version.note: No ResearchArena repo. The pinned commit 228791fb499a belongs to karpathy/autoresearch, a different system.

stars.note: The 96348 stars belong to karpathy/autoresearch, not ResearchArena.
